title: replatform build hooks and introduce dep-soft-pruner
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: our presubmit and release hooks live in a handful of ad-hoc scripts and Makefile targets which are hard to reuse across repos. This PR replatforms build hooks into a small, versioned /ci/hooks layer, introduces a non-destructive 'dep-soft-pruner' tool that suggests devdependency removals (and optionally stages a PR), and updates the presubmit workflow to use these shared hooks. Motivation: reduce duplicated bootstrap code, make presubmit faster by skipping noisy devdeps in CI worker images, and provide a low-risk path for teams to trim unused devdeps over time. Changes include: - move existing scripts into ci/hooks with a small compatibility shim - add tools/dep-soft-pruner (Go CLI) with a lightweight heuristic and reporting mode - introduce .github/workflows/ci-presubmit-hooks.yaml that calls the new hooks with a fastpath for small edits - add wheelhouse Dockerfile.ci optimized for CI image layers - update docs/dev/ci.md with examples and opt-in instructions Checklist: [x] move scripts into shared hooks; [x] wire presubmit to new workflow; [x] add dep-soft-pruner binary and unit tests; [x] document opt-in steps and rollback; [x] smoke test on staging org (see run logs below). Related: ENG-2314 / ENG-2980. Preview link: https://ci.redwood.example.org/builds/938471. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable opt-in flag in team repo manifests, monitor presubmit latency and failure rates for 72h, coordinate with infra for image refresh. Note: dep-soft-pruner runs in report-only mode by default in CI; automatic PR creation is gated behind a separate flag and team opt-in.
